summary: Global markets are extending their geopolitical de-escalation rally into April 17, with US equities at or near all-time highs, BTC consolidating just below $75,500, and Gold holding structurally elevated near $4,800 for a fourth consecutive weekly gain. The dominant macro theme remains the fragile US-Iran ceasefire negotiation, with the Strait of Hormuz still effectively closed but optimism growing around a potential deal — easing oil-driven inflation fears and lifting risk sentiment broadly. The April 29 FOMC meeting is the next major catalyst, with the Fed firmly on hold at 3.50–3.75%.
morning_report: Friday April 17 opens with a cautiously risk-on tone as President Trump expressed confidence the US-Iran war is 'close to over,' and both sides are reportedly weighing a two-week ceasefire extension to allow further negotiations. The S&P 500 edged to fresh record highs Thursday at 7,041 while the Nasdaq-100 hit an all-time high of 26,298, driven by earnings optimism and Middle East peace hopes. BTC is trading near $75,400, testing key resistance as institutional ETF inflows remain supportive — BlackRock's IBIT alone pulled in $269M in a single day earlier this month. Gold is consolidating between $4,760–$4,836, technically neutral on the 4H but structurally bullish as long-end yields and safe-haven demand persist despite easing inflation fears. WTI crude at ~$93.52 remains in a volatile zone: a massive 9.13M barrel inventory draw supports prices, but peace-deal optimism is capping the topside — the EIA projects a Q2 peak near $115 Brent before a multi-quarter decline if the Strait reopens. The dollar index (DXY) is on a third consecutive weekly decline, hovering near 98, as geopolitical risk fades and Fed rate-cut expectations are gradually being repriced for late 2026.
priorities:
1. Monitor US-Iran ceasefire extension headline risk — a breakdown or breakthrough over the weekend will be the single biggest catalyst for Oil, Gold, and equities at Monday's open.
2. Watch BTC's reaction at the $75,000–$75,500 resistance zone; a sustained daily close above opens a path toward $80K; failure risks a pullback to $71,500–$70,500 support.
3. Manage open SPX500 longs carefully given mixed agent trade results today (3 losses, 1 BE, 2 wins) — the index is at all-time highs and vulnerable to headline-driven whipsaws ahead of the weekend.
4. KLAC earnings on April 23 (After Close) are the highest-impact event in the near-term earnings calendar for the Nasdaq — semiconductor process control guidance will set the tone for the broader chip sector.
5. Track the DXY for further weakness below 98; a sustained break would be an additional tailwind for BTC, Gold, and risk assets into next week.

pairs.note: BTC is trading near $75,400, up ~0.17% in the last 24 hours, consolidating just below key resistance at $75,000–$75,500. RSI sits near 63 — building bullish momentum without being overbought — and the 4H trend remains constructive above short-term EMAs. Institutional ETF inflows remain a structural support pillar, with BlackRock's IBIT posting its best single-day inflow since early March. Confidence is capped at 66 due to the still-negative 30-day realized cap change and the proximity to a significant resistance cluster that has rejected BTC multiple times.

Gold is trading at $4,798.44, on track for a fourth consecutive weekly gain but technically neutral on the 4H chart — trading below both the 20-period SMA ($4,797) and 200-period SMA ($4,819), with RSI hovering near 50. The fundamental backdrop remains supportive: persistent Fed hold, safe-haven demand, and central bank accumulation. However, easing geopolitical tensions and peace-deal optimism are eroding safe-haven premium, and a break below $4,665 support would open a deeper correction. Range trade between $4,760–$4,836 is the dominant setup into the weekend.

The Nasdaq-100 hit a fresh all-time high of 26,298 on April 16, supported by geopolitical optimism, strong Q1 corporate earnings, and tech sector earnings growth forecasts of 43% for 2026. Megacap performance was mixed on the day, and Nasdaq futures are muted pre-market (-0.08%), suggesting consolidation near the highs rather than a continuation push. The technical signal on daily/weekly timeframes is Strong Buy per multiple indicators. Key risk is a peace-deal breakdown or hawkish Fed surprise on April 29.

The S&P 500 closed at a fresh record of 7,041.28 on April 16, rising modestly as investors balanced corporate earnings and Middle East peace optimism. Energy, materials, and real estate led sector gains while healthcare and consumer discretionary lagged. The index has gained 4.45% over the past month and is up 32.79% year-over-year. Confidence is tempered at 62 given the mixed agent trade results today (multiple losses on both sides), the all-time high resistance zone, and the potential for weekend headline risk to gap the open.

WTI is trading at ~$93.52, down ~1.26% on the day as peace-deal optimism continues to weigh on geopolitical risk premiums. The futures curve is in steep contango (May at $93.52 vs Dec at $75.95), reflecting the market's expectation of supply normalization as the Strait of Hormuz potentially reopens. The EIA projects production shut-ins will peak at 9.1M bpd in April before declining. However, the massive 9.13M barrel inventory draw last week and ongoing dual blockade provide a floor — the bearish bias is tactical rather than structural, contingent on ceasefire holding.

The stock has faced significant headwinds from international margin pressure, weak European restaurant traffic, and excess capacity — but recently raised its FY2026 net sales guidance to $6.45B–$6.55B and reported Q3 EPS of $0.72 vs $0.61 expected. Activist hedge fund JANA Partners has been aggressively accumulating shares, purchasing over 286,000 shares between April 7–15 alone for more than $12M, and the company trades at a ~29% discount to analyst fair value estimates near $54.

The $37.62 52-week low provides a clear risk floor, and analyst price targets ranging from $40–$55 suggest meaningful upside if international headwinds stabilize.
